text:
Winnipeg arrives on a four-game winning streak, the latest a 4-2 win over New Jersey that ended the Devils' five-game run. The Jets are still without Elias Salomonsson and Vladislav Namestnikov. Dallas, rested after four days off, beat San Jose 4-3 last time out, but is missing Miro Heiskanen. Since he went out, Thomas Harley has moved onto the first power-play unit and Tyler Myers has gone up to 20:08 a night from 17:10. These two met Oct 22, and Dallas won 3-2 in overtime.

At five on five, the Jets have taken 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in their games and the Stars 52%, so there isn't much between them. Our numbers say the Jets are better than their record, with finishing costing them. The special-teams matchup to watch is Dallas's power play (0.78 expected goals a game) against Winnipeg's penalty kill (0.84 allowed). Dallas has taken 4.1 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays. In net, projected starter Stuart Skinner sits at +0.4 goals saved above expected (a measure of saves beyond what the shots should produce), while Jake Oettinger is at +7.7. Last season it was +5.96 for Skinner and +2.15 for Oettinger. Our model has Dallas at 3.22 expected goals tonight and Winnipeg at 2.66.

Kyle Connor is our top Jets scorer at 42%, and Mark Scheifele has a four-game point streak. For Dallas, Wyatt Johnston and Jason Robertson are both at 38% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Tyler Seguin, a third-liner at about 14:11 a night whose shots have been dangerous: 2.9 expected goals in his last 10 games. We have him at 21% to score. He's a player to watch, not a lock.
